Subject: POC trial planning: AcmeHealth workload intake and next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the trial plan: 

Recap from discovery:
- Primary use: clinical note summarization for provider workflow (high precision, low hallucination tolerance)
- Priority KPI: reduce time-to-summary and maintain >98% accuracy on key fields
- Data: de-identified sample payloads available from your side (JSON), up to ~50k records for validation

Proposed POC / trial plan (high-level):
1) Workload intake: you fill the attached workload template with RPS, token lengths, concurrency, and sample payloads by EOD Thu 3/25.
2) Trial environment: 2-week trial in Redwood Dedicated (isolated GPU pool). Target start: Mon 4/4.
3) Success criteria (draft):
   - p95 generation latency < 300ms for < 256-token outputs
   - End-to-end error rate < 1%
   - Quality: automated checks + manual eval pass rate >= 95% on the evaluation set
4) Ownership:
   - Acme: Alex (engineering lead) + Priya (clinical QA) for data and quality signoff
   - Redwood: Ben (AM) + Marissa (SE) for infra, tuning, and eval harness setup
5) Deliverables before start:
   - Completed workload template (attached)
   - Sample payloads (de-identified) uploaded/shared
   - Shared Drive planning doc created (link below)

Immediate asks for you: please confirm the proposed start date (4/4) and fill the attached template with the following fields: avg RPS, peak RPS, avg/max input tokens, avg/max output tokens, typical concurrency, burst patterns (time-of-day), and any soft real-time SLAs.

I've attached the workload intake template (acme_health_poc_workload_template.xlsx) and linked the draft plan in Drive. Once you send the workload numbers, Marissa will size the trial compute and propose a concrete config and cost for the 2-week run.

Thanks — look forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Ben

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers to the workload fields while we complete the template: 

- Typical avg RPS: 2 requests/sec
- Typical peak RPS: 60 requests/sec during morning ingest windows
- Typical concurrency: 4 concurrent requests (background batch processing), bursts up to ~50 concurrent for short windows (5-10m)
- Avg input tokens: 120 tokens (clinical notes), max input tokens: ~1,200 (rare)
- Avg output tokens: 40 tokens, max output tokens: 200
- Traffic pattern: sharp spike 07:00-09:30 PST, smaller spike 16:30-18:00 PST, steady low traffic overnight
- Data: we can provide ~10k de-identified records for initial eval; clinical QA team will review outputs

I attached a small sample payload file (sample_payloads.json) and I'll get the completed template back to you by Thu 3/25 as requested. Start date 4/4 looks fine from our side.

One note on SLA: we need clarity on how Redwood handles model fallbacks during capacity limits — we prefer graceful degradation (cached summaries / rate-limited calls) over failing requests.

Alex
Senior Eng Manager, Platform Integrations
AcmeHealth

Subject: Re: POC trial planning: AcmeHealth workload intake and next steps

Great — this is super helpful, Alex. Based on the numbers you shared, here are the recommended initial trial sizing and evaluation plan items: 

Trial sizing (initial recommendation):
- Dedicated pool: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved for 2-week window) with autoscaling to 3x for short bursts
- Batching strategy: continuous batching with 250ms max batch delay to balance latency and throughput
- KV/prefix cache: enabled for repeated prompts (saves ~15-20% token compute in our tests)
- Quantization: run int8 profile for cost efficiency; we’ll validate quality drop-in with your eval set

Success criteria (finalize during kickoff):
- Latency: p95 < 350ms for <=256-token outputs (we'll aim for 300ms but allow headroom)
- Reliability: API error rate < 1% and <=2% degraded responses (fallback to smaller model or cached result)
- Quality: manual eval >=95% on the acceptance set; automated QA checks for hallucination rate and entity recall

Evaluation plan / timeline:
- Thu 3/25: Acme returns workload template + sample payloads
- Mon 3/29: Redwood will produce a sizing and cost quote + trial playbook (config, test routes, monitoring setup)
- Mon 4/4: Kickoff + deploy trial environment
- Weeks 1-2 (4/4 - 4/17): Run trial, daily smoke checks, mid-trial checkpoint on 4/11
- 4/18-4/21: Final evaluation, QA signoff, and decision meeting

Operational notes re: fallbacks: we support policy-based routing — during capacity limits we can route to: 1) cached responses for identical requests, 2) smaller/cheaper model variants, or 3) rate-limit non-critical routes. We'll include a proposed fallback policy in the trial playbook.

Can you confirm the sample payloads above are fully de-identified and that Priya is OK with the proposed evaluation windows? Once confirmed, Marissa will size the infra and share a formal quote by 3/29.

Thanks — looping Marissa for the infra sizing and playbook.

Ben
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
